title: Allocate by the stated weight
hook: Three trays have weights 2:1:1. Does an equal split follow those weights?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Allocate a conserved volume according to stated relative weights.

misconception: An equal split satisfies every weighted allocation rule.
objective: Allocate a conserved volume according to stated relative weights.

claims.text: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1. Compare volume assigned to the first tray. Scaled model; empty trays; arithmetic allocation only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Total=8L, A=4L and B=2.667L. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Total. At x=8, A=4, B=2.66666666667; recall at x=11: B=3.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: The weights add to four. The first tray receives two of four units, or half the total. Splitting into three equal shares uses a different rule and produces a different allocation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Total. At x=8, A=4, B=2.66666666667; recall at x=11: B=3.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1. Compare volume assigned to the first tray. Change only Total to 11L. What is B (Equal) now? Correct: 3.667L. Use B's stated rule with Total=11L: it gives 3.667L. The weights add to four. The first tray receives two of four units, or half the total. Splitting into three equal shares uses a different rule and produces a different allocation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Total. At x=8, A=4, B=2.66666666667; recall at x=11: B=3.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1. Compare volume assigned to the first tray. Change only Total to 11L. What is B (Equal) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Total=11L: it gives 3.667L. The weights add to four. The first tray receives two of four units, or half the total. Splitting into three equal shares uses a different rule and produces a different allocation.

safety.assumptions: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1. Compare volume assigned to the first tray.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
